block_definition: The pre-registered EXTENSION RULE (screen_protocol.md sec.3.1) continues into the reserve in permutation order in blocks of 50 until 75 included papers are reached or position 400 is exhausted. R3 is the third such block: permutation positions 211-260 inclusive, 50 records, taken in permutation order with no substitution and no truncation. Every PMID was re-checked against screen_sample.json position-by-position before coding.
screener_id_note: Reserve blocks are worked by a single operator against the amended codebook; the reserve records at 211-260 carry pre-assigned round-robin batch labels A/B/C/D in screen_sample.json, preserved in each record's 'reserve_assigned_to' field. 'screener_id' is set to S3 because the operator coded this block alone; the value is NOT a claim of independent multi-rater coding, and NONE of these records enters any agreement statistic. independence_statement: Coded from the primary sources only. No other screener's codes were consulted; screen_batch_{A,B,C,D}.json, screen_recoded.json, screen_reserve_R1.json, screen_reserve_R2.json and screen/access_recovery.json were not opened for any record in this block. screen_frame.json v1.2 and screen_protocol.md were read IN FULL BEFORE any record in this block was read, as the task required. The 50 records were taken from screen_sample.json by permutation position, not by any property of the papers.
access_ladder_note: screen_protocol.md sec.7 rungs attempted in order for every record that reached stage 2: (1) PubMed Central / Europe PMC / publisher OA; (2) the publisher's own site; (3) institutional subscription -- NOT available to this operator, recorded as such rather than left implicit; (4) institutional repository, accepted manuscript or preprint, located via Unpaywall, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC fullTextUrlList/title search, OpenAIRE and arXiv; (5) interlibrary loan / direct author request -- cannot complete inside one session and the protocol's 21-day clock cannot elapse, so records failing rungs 1-4 are coded unreachable_paywalled rather than left pending. That is the honest and the conservative code. Per D4 the ladder was NOT climbed for the 7 CLOSED-ACCESS records excluded at stage 1; those are coded not_attempted_excluded_at_stage1 so that endpoint S6 measures the reachability of the eligible-looking literature only. For the 7 stage-1 exclusions that happened to be in PMC, D4's second sentence applies and the rung that worked is recorded, because the full text was in hand and was used to verify the exclusion code.
sources_refused: Sci-Hub, LibGen and every other unauthorised full-text source. None was accessed and no record is reported as reachable because one of them holds it. Bot-detection and JavaScript challenges were NOT circumvented: link.springer.com and nature.com served a 'Client Challenge' interstitial for PMIDs 41361534, 33428062 and 38433144, and journals.sagepub.com, pubs.acs.org, onlinelibrary.wiley.com, pubs.rsna.org and sciencedirect.com returned HTTP 403; all are recorded as failed rungs and all those records stay unreachable.
supplement_policy: reading_effort.stage_2_required_searches requires the 14 terms to be run over the supplement as well as the main text. For every included record this file states, in searches_run, one of: (a) the supplement was obtained and searched, naming the file; (b) the article declares no supplementary material, so none exists; or (c) a supplement is declared but could not be obtained, in which case the record is flagged. Exactly ONE included record falls under (c): PMID 42433232, whose only declared attachments are administrative (TRIPOD reporting checklist, COI form, data-sharing statement, peer-review file) and which Europe PMC serves as HTTP 404 while PMC serves a download interstitial. Supplements were retrieved through the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint; PDFs were read with PyMuPDF and .docx/.xlsx with a ZIP/XML reader.
coding_conventions_applied: R3-A. Every hit on every one of the 14 terms was READ, not counted. Six would have produced a FALSE P1 OR S1 POSITIVE if counted: PMID 31941918's 'Majority Voting rule (MVR)' is a seven-CNN ensemble aggregation, not a majority-class predictor; PMID 39369213's '95% permutation interval' is a permutation-based confidence interval on the model's own AUC, not a permuted-label null; PMID 37960407's 'Adam and SGD are chosen as two baselines' are OPTIMISERS; PMID 33846450's 'the highest accuracy permutation of the pre-training and augmentation variations' is an experimental grid; PMID 41767013's 'ResNet baseline 46 ms' is an inference-time comparison; PMID 38988988's 'Majority Voting method, namely KNNRF-DT' describes another paper's ensemble.

R3-B. The one genuine near-miss is coded FALSE and the reason is on the record. PMID 40338065 reports a model labelled 'Cli' with a measured AUC of 0.712/0.690 and a legend reading 'clinical imaging model'. Its surviving features are Age, Cirrhosis, AFP and INTRATUMOR VASCULARITY -- a radiologist-read imaging sign -- so it is not pixel-free and clinical_or_demographic_only is FALSE. The codebook requires 'patient variables only ... with no imaging'. Coding it TRUE would have put an S1 positive on the board cheaply and would have been wrong.

R3-C. E-DERIV vs include, the line drawn identically to reserve block R2's convention R2-C: E-DERIV where the FITTED CLASSIFIER's input is a hand-crafted or otherwise non-spatial feature vector and no network ingests pixels for the class decision (PMIDs 41877097, 42279183, 35500505, 40870922, 40038938); INCLUDE where a fitted deep network ingests the image itself even if a classical or shallow classifier sits on top of its activations (PMIDs 40338065, 42433232, 37770730).

R3-D. TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS ON CRITERION I3 DRIVE THE DENOMINATOR AND ARE BOTH FLAGGED. PMIDs 39166052 (Zeiss Visante AS-OCT, four discrete meridional B-scans per eye) and 40478199 (UK Biobank liver MRI, ONE 10 mm transverse slice per participant) use a volumetric-capable modality acquired as a single cross-section, not as 'an ordered stack of 2D cross-sections' (criterion I3), so there is no slice axis. Both are excluded E-2D on that code's HEADLINE rule ('Imaging is natively 2D'), because the codebook has no code for this case and E-2D's example list contains only natively-2D modalities. The 14-term search WAS run on both, main text and supplement: neither reports a zero-image baseline, so the sensitivity analysis is exact -- including both gives P1 = 0/21 = 0.0% [0.0%, 15.5%] and S6 = 9/30 = 30.0%, and the block's primary result does not move.

R3-E. evaluation_unit_reported is coded 'unclear' wherever the paper counts only 'images', 'cases' or 'samples' and never states whether one such unit is one cross-section or one subject/volume (4 of 19 included records). 'slice' is coded only where the paper says slice / B-scan / axial slice or its split table's own column header does. Naming a 2D architecture is NOT treated as a statement about the scored unit.

R3-F. trivial_baseline sub-flags on records that were NOT included: 'not_applicable' where final_inclusion='excluded' (D3), and 'not_assessable' where final_inclusion='unreachable_eligibility_unresolved' (D2c), with the failed rung named in trivial_baseline_quote for all nine unreachable records. Both levels are outside every P1 and S1 numerator and denominator. Not one FALSE is entered anywhere without the 14-term search behind it.
